title: Self-service sign-up: a stranger asks for a workspace, with no manual or infra step
description: The owner's acceptance scenario (T-2749, G10b, acceptance map item 11 'self-service demo tenant'). The runner calls the PUBLIC sign-up routes without a token (actor 'anonymous'), with a throwaway address in the mail trap (Mailpit) and a uat-tmp-* company name. Part 1 (this file, runs on today's build): S1 the sign-up is switched on and its config is public; S2 a request without accepted terms is refused 422 invalid_request naming terms_accepted; S3 a request with a malformed address is refused 422; S4 a good request is answered 202 check_your_mail; S5 the verification mail reaches the trap (wait_mail: the body and the token never reach the log). Part 2 (see later_steps) needs the sign-up fields slug, user name and password of T-2748 and the one-time provisioner wiring on QA: until they exist the scenario is RED with a named reason (sign-up not enabled, or provisioner not configured), which is the expected red and no defect. D-195: the scenario goes from the sign-up to a signed-in tenant admin with no step that waits for a human; a step that does is a defect and a red scenario, named in the verdict line. No qoimeks-qa or qoimeks-client1-qa tenant is touched. The verification link is opened by the SPA page, so the runner does not read the body of the mail. Part 2 is executable (T-2749 rework): S6 posts the full sign-up (company name, user name, password from the input signup_password, slug uat-tmp-<run_id>) and expects 202 with the tenant URL; S7 the platform administrator reads the registry entry and expects it ACTIVE with no human step (D-195); S8 slug taken and S9 reserved slug are refused; the cleanup deactivates ONLY the tenant uat-tmp-<run_id> and the platform residue check (actor admin on the platform tenant) fails the run on a leftover active uat-tmp-* tenant. Until the sign-up fields (T-2748) and the provisioner wiring exist S6 or S7 is RED with the reason 'sign-up fields not supported / provisioner not configured': the expected red. The demo-cap refusal and the sign-in as the new tenant administrator (a token of a realm that exists only after the run starts) are not executable by the runner today (L3, L4b in later_steps).
later_steps: L3: sign in as the NEW tenant admin (token of the new realm, no secret in the log) and GET /api/v1/me answers 200 with the role TENANT_ADMIN: needs a runner login step for a realm created at run time; until then the scenario does not claim it
L4b: the demo cap reached is refused with a closed reason: needs the cap filled, not executable without side effects on a shared QA
L5b: purge of the tenant after the deactivation, only when T-2747 exists

inputs.signup_password: <set by the starter at run time>

steps.says: Anyone may read the public sign-up config: it is switched on and offers the three languages. If it answers 404 the sign-up is not enabled on this build: RED, reason 'sign-up not enabled'.
A request that does not accept the terms is refused 422 and names the field.
A good request is answered 202 check_your_mail, whether or not the address is known.
The verification mail reaches the throwaway address in the mail trap, with no human step. Only recipient, subject and message id are read.

The full sign-up: company name, user name, password, desired slug. Answered 202 with the tenant URL of the new workspace. RED here means the build lacks the sign-up fields (T-2748) or the provisioner is not configured.
With no human step the new tenant exists and is ACTIVE (the platform administrator reads the registry entry). D-195: if it waits for a person it is RED.
The slug is taken: a second sign-up for the same slug is refused with the code slug_taken.
A reserved word as the slug is refused 422.

cleanup.says: Deactivate only the throwaway tenant this run made (its slug starts with uat-tmp-).
